transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. 

Um, well, I guess what made me call the EAP is that lately... every little bang in the office is really getting to me. Like, if a file drawer shuts loud or someone drops a coffee mug, I just jump really hard. And then my chest keeps racing for way longer than it should after something like that happens. It's just been bothering me enough that I figured I should come in.
Have you been through something traumatic that still feels upsetting to you now?

Yeah, there was an incident at the office a little while ago. I had a situation with one of the guys I supervise that got really out of hand. 

I remember him slamming a chair down and then standing right in front of the door so I couldn't get out. But... it's strange, when I try to explain the worst part of it, the actual words he was yelling at me are just completely blank. It's like that specific section just got cut out of my memory. But yeah, even without remembering exactly what he said, the whole thing definitely still upsets me.
Do unwanted memories of that incident ever suddenly pop into your mind when you don't want them to?

No, not really. Um, I don't think so, anyway. I mean, obviously I think about it when something reminds me of it—like when there's a loud noise in the office, like I mentioned. But... no, I don't really have memories of it just randomly popping into my head out of nowhere when I'm trying to do other things.
Have you been avoiding that part of the office or interactions with that employee because they remind you of what happened?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I still have to work in that same area, so I can't really avoid it. And as for him... well, he got fired right after it happened, so he's not around anymore. I don't really have to worry about running into him or anything. So, no, I haven't really been avoiding anything specific like that.
Outside of reminders of that office incident, do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, sure, I have normal stress with work and life, but I'm not, like, constantly worrying about a bunch of different things all the time. It's really just that one situation at the office that's been bothering me.
Do you ever have sudden episodes of intense fear or physical panic that seem to come on out of the blue?
No, I haven't really had anything like that. I mean, I get a little jumpy sometimes, like I said, but I haven't had any sudden, intense panic attacks or anything that just comes out of nowhere.
Have these reactions been going on for more than a month since that incident happened?
No, it hasn't been a month. It's been about two weeks, actually. It all started right after that late-night confrontation with my regional boss. So, yeah, just about two weeks.
Since this started, have you been feeling down or depressed?

No, not really. I don't think I've felt depressed. I mean, I'm definitely shaken up and stressed about what happened, but my mood overall hasn't been, you know, down or sad or anything like that. It's really just the stress of dealing with that one night.
